## Summary

DENSO Corporation is a Japanese automotive components maker
headquartered in Kariya, Aichi, founded in 1949 as Nippon Denso Co.,
Ltd. and renamed in 1996; it belongs to the Toyota Group, with Toyota
Motor Corporation holding 21.25% and Toyota Industries 5.59% [1]. Its
products include engine components, hybrid vehicle components, climate
control, instrument clusters, airbag systems, pre-crash radar and spark
plugs, and its subsidiary Denso Wave created the QR code in 1994 [1].
The IEEE registry lists two MA-L blocks to "DENSO CORPORATION" at the
Kariya head office [2].

Which DENSO product carries a MAC from these blocks is not documented
by the sources consulted, so device classes, radios and products are
left unknown rather than guessed [1][2]. The registry's other DENSO
spellings ("DENSO Co.,Ltd" in Osaka, "Denso Manufacturing Tennessee",
"FUJITSU DENSO LTD.", "Nippon Denso Industry Co., Ltd.") are not
aliased here, since the sources do not tie them to this company [2].
An NVD keyword search for DENSO returned only CVE-2025-57781, which
concerns installers for a DENSO TEN drive recorder viewer, not a
networked product tied to these blocks, so no security note is
recorded [3]. DENSO's own site and the
FCC ID databases refused the session that wrote this entry, so silicon
and grantee codes are not listed.
